title: src/lua/ (14 files, LUA-01..16 all RELEASED) is unreferenced by the build graph and no longer compiles under Zig 0.16
notes:
Discovered while resolving ISS-0147 / GH #463 (the src/wasm equivalent). src/lua/ is the sibling scripting subsystem and is in the identical unreferenced state, but with worse rot and a harder blocker.

EVIDENCE OF UNREFERENCEDNESS:
- No `b.createModule` in build.zig has any src/lua file as root (grep -n -i lua build.zig returns only unrelated expr/DSL lines plus the test-misc-unit step description).
- Neither src/bpm.zig nor src/main.zig imports it.
- No addTest root reaches it. It carries zero in-file `test` blocks, so tools/lint_test_wiring.py does NOT flag it (that linter only tracks test-bearing files) -- this is invisible to the existing gate, exactly as src/wasm was.
- Single commit in history: 113bdb3 'Stage 9', never touched since.

EVIDENCE OF ROT (would fail to compile the moment it is analysed):
- `c_void` is used in src/lua/executor.zig:178, luajit_bindings.zig:40,66,83,121 and memory_limiter.zig:30. `c_void` was renamed to `anyopaque` in Zig 0.11; this repo is on Zig 0.16.
- `callconv(.C)` is used in 12 places across executor.zig, instruction_limiter.zig, memory_limiter.zig, luajit_bindings.zig and all 8 host_api/*.zig files. Zig 0.16 made CallingConvention a tagged union whose C member is lowercase `.c`. This is the same defect fixed in src/wasm/wasmtime_bindings.zig:70 under ISS-0147.

HARDER THAN ISS-0147 -- REAL EXTERNAL LINK REQUIRED:
Unlike src/wasm (whose wasmtime_bindings.zig is pure `extern struct` layout types plus `inline fn` stubs, needing no link), src/lua/luajit_bindings.zig declares real `pub extern fn lua_*` symbols AND does `@cImport` of the LuaJIT headers. Wiring src/lua into a build target therefore requires an actual LuaJIT dependency (linkSystemLibrary or a vendored build), which is a genuine infrastructure decision -- not a mechanical wiring change. That is why this is filed separately rather than fixed inline alongside ISS-0147.

RISK: 16 MUST requirements (LUA-01..16) are marked RELEASED in docs/requirements.yaml with `implemented_in` pointing at these files, but the code they point at cannot currently be compiled at all. The RELEASED status is not backed by anything executable.
candidate_resolution: Decide liveness of src/lua the same way ISS-0147 decided it for src/wasm. If live: (a) resolve the LuaJIT link story (vendor it, or linkSystemLibrary behind a build flag defaulting off), (b) fix the c_void -> anyopaque and callconv(.C) -> callconv(.c) rot, (c) declare a lua module in build.zig and re-export it via src/bpm.zig by NAME (src/lua files reach siblings by relative path, so the Single-Owner Module Rule applies as it did for src/wasm), (d) add a reachability test mirroring tests/unit/wasm_reexport_test.zig. If NOT live: downgrade LUA-01..16 from RELEASED to a status that reflects reality, and delete or documented-exclude the directory. Either way the current state -- RELEASED requirements pointing at non-compiling unreferenced code -- must not persist.
resolution: Repaired src/lua's Zig 0.16 rot and wired the subsystem into the build graph; corrected the dishonest requirement status. LUAJIT LINK VERDICT: NOT AVAILABLE, verified empirically -- a probe containing only @cInclude("lua.h") fails with 'lua.h not found' with and without -lc; `zig test -lc -lluajit-5.1` fails with 'unable to find dynamic system library'; no lua.h/libluajit anywhere on disk; vendor/ and build.zig.zon .dependencies contain only pg/http/cel; nothing in docker-compose.yml or .github/workflows/. Therefore option (b) of the issue's own acceptance criteria was taken, matching ISS-0147's disposition for src/wasm: luajit_bindings.zig's unresolvable @cImport + `pub extern fn lua_*` surface was replaced with pure-Zig `inline fn` stubs carrying the faithful LuaJIT 2.1 ABI shape, so the subsystem compiles and is type-checked with no linker involvement. Stubs return FAILURE sentinels (lua_newstate -> null, luaL_loadstring -> LUA_ERRSYNTAX, lua_pcall -> LUA_ERRRUN), never success, so executeScript reports an error rather than pretending to run a script; `has_real_luajit = false` is asserted by a test. ROT FIXED (8 categories, only 2 of which the issue had identified): c_void -> anyopaque (5 sites); callconv(.C) -> callconv(.c) (12 sites); two-argument @ptrCast -> single-arg (4 sites); `&&` -> `and` in host_api/fail.zig; std.time.nanoTimestamp() (removed in 0.16) -> a portable currentNanoTimestamp() mirroring src/api/routes/instances.zig's established pattern; `{:04d}` -> `{d:0>4}` format syntax (2 files); three decls called but never declared (lua_istable, lua_sethook, lua_Debug); and ScriptValue.deinit, which did not compile AND would have leaked the HashMap and invited a double free -- rewritten as a single recursive pass. timeout.zig's @divExact on elapsed nanoseconds (which panics for any non-whole-millisecond duration) became @divTrunc with a backwards-clock clamp. WIRING: new addTest root src/lua_test_root.zig at src/ (NOT src/lua/ -- host_api/*.zig reaches ../../simulation/, which reaches ../event_store/store.zig, so an inside-src/lua root is rejected with 'import of file outside module path'; verified empirically). New `zig build test-lua` target, attached to the aggregate `test` step. src/lua/mod.zig is deliberately NOT a named-module root and NOT re-exported from bpm.zig (documented there), because src/simulation and src/event_store are already owned by bpm_src_mod -- the Single-Owner Module Rule. Reachability was proven by MUTATION: a type error injected into the body of get_instance_state.platformGetInstanceState turned the target red, confirming analysis descends into nested function bodies rather than stopping at refAllDecls' shallow container walk. 11 tests execute and pass. STATUS CORRECTION: all 16 of LUA-01..16 downgraded RELEASED -> IN_PROGRESS, since RELEASED was not backed by anything executable. LUA-04 was downgraded too despite its bytecode-magic rejection being genuine pure-Zig logic with a passing test, because its defence-in-depth also depends on stdlib.zig stripping load/loadstring from a real interpreter, which runs against stubs and is unverified. GATES: zig build exit 0 with no 'error set' output; zig build test exit 0 (837 tests across 30 targets); python tools/lint_test_wiring.py exit 0. The remaining half -- actually linking LuaJIT so scripts execute -- is filed as ISS-0161 / GH #485 and enqueued.
prevention: The blind spot that hid this for three months: tools/lint_test_wiring.py only tracks test-BEARING files, so a subsystem with zero `test` blocks is invisible to it no matter how unreferenced it is. src/wasm (ISS-0147) and src/lua (this issue) were both found by hand, not by a gate, and a third such directory would be found the same way. The durable fix is a check for source directories under src/ that no addTest root and no module declaration reaches -- reachability of CODE, not just of tests. Until that exists, adding a test root (as done here) is what keeps a subsystem honest: it converts silent rot into a red build. Second lesson, and the reason the fix took 8 rot categories rather than the 2 the issue named: an unanalysed file accumulates errors in every category the language changes, not just the ones someone happened to grep for. Do not scope this kind of repair from a grep count -- compile it and read what the compiler actually says. Third: when wiring a previously-dead subsystem, prove the wiring with a deliberate mutation before declaring it done. A green run proves nothing when the tests may not be running at all (docs/anti-patterns.md, ISS-0133). refAllDecls in particular is shallow over containers, so 'it compiles' and 'its function bodies are analysed' are different claims. Fourth: a stub standing in for a missing runtime must return a FAILURE sentinel, never success. A permissive stub is the ISS-0155 silent-false-negative pattern -- it makes callers, reviewers and status files all read as working. Pair it with a public `has_real_luajit`-style constant that a test asserts against, so the pretence cannot drift back in unnoticed. Fifth: RELEASED must mean 'backed by something executable'. Sixteen MUST requirements sat RELEASED against code that could not be compiled at all. Before setting RELEASED, confirm the implementing files are reachable from a build target that actually runs.
